subject: Per-token discounts and marketplace pass-throughs — Acme AI
messages:
From: Procurement - Acme AI <procurement@acme.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: AWS Marketplace Partner Sales <aws-partner-sales@amazon.com>
Date: 2027-06-06T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarification on per-token discounts via AWS Marketplace vs Direct

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — Acme is excited about Redwood's latency profile and the per-token model for our embedding-heavy workload. Before we move to contract we need clarity on two points from procurement:

1) If we purchase via AWS Marketplace, how should we expect the advertised per-token discount to map to the net price we pay once AWS listing fees and marketplace pass-through arrangements are applied?
2) Does Redwood provide a gross-to-net adjustment or credit so that commit tiers translate to the same effective unit economics whether billed directly or through a cloud marketplace?

We are considering a 12-month commit, starting at 25M tokens/month. Our internal finance team needs an estimate of the net per-token rate (USD) on both paths so we can compare TCO.

Could you put together a short worked example (list price, Redwood discount, marketplace fee, net price) and confirm whether DocuSign routing via AWS Marketplace is supported?

Appreciate it — procurement is on a tight window this quarter.

Best,
Maya Rao
Procurement Lead
Acme AI

Attachments: none
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Procurement - Acme AI <procurement@acme.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, AWS Marketplace Partner Sales <aws-partner-sales@amazon.com>
Date: 2027-06-06T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on per-token discounts via AWS Marketplace vs Direct

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear ask and for the time last week. Looping in Neha (sales) and Rishi (pricing/finance) so we can give you a concise worked example and confirm DocuSign routing.

Short answer up front: the headline discounts on our hosted API apply to Redwood's list price. Marketplace billing introduces a platform fee (varies by provider) that typically reduces the net discount seen by the customer unless we apply a gross-to-net credit on our side. We have a few standard approaches depending on procurement constraints:

- Direct billing (preferred for clean unit economics): customer billed by Redwood; standard tiered per-token discounts apply.
- Marketplace billing (AWS/GCP/Azure): provider fee is added on top of Redwood's charge and is generally non-negotiable; in some cases we make a margin adjustment (credit) to preserve the effective unit price for the customer — this is handled on a case-by-case basis and requires finance approval.

I attached a quick quote and a spreadsheet that breaks the math out by tier. Proposed next steps:
1) Neha/Rishi — can you confirm the example numbers (I attached RIF-Commit-Quote-v2.pdf and Marketplace-Fee-Impact.xlsx) and indicate whether we can offer a marketplace credit for ACME's 25M/month 12-month commit?
2) Maya — if the numbers look ok I can route a DocuSign either directly (Redwood -> Acme) or via AWS Marketplace (Redwood -> AWS -> Acme). Note: DocuSign via AWS adds a step on marketplace reconciliation and may delay invoice timing.

Proposed call: Thu 10 AM PT to finalize.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RIF-Commit-Quote-v2.pdf, Marketplace-Fee-Impact.xlsx
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement - Acme AI <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: 2027-06-07T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on per-token discounts via AWS Marketplace vs Direct

Tessa / Rishi — dug into the numbers and documented the assumptions in the attached spreadsheet. Key points below (worked example for Acme's 25M tokens/month commit):

Assumptions:
- Redwood list price (hosted API) = $0.00040 per token
- Committed discount at 25M/month = 30% off list (negotiated level)
- AWS Marketplace fee that effectively reduces vendor payout = 12% (partner referral/listing + handling)
- Sales tax / VAT not modeled in example (depends on Acme's nexus)

Worked math (per token):
- List price: $0.00040
- Redwood post-discount (direct billing): $0.00028 (30% off)
- If sold via AWS Marketplace without credit: AWS adds the fee/marketplace surcharge to the customer-facing price, so the buyer pays roughly $0.00028 / (1 - 0.12) = $0.000318 per token (this is a simplified pass-through view). Effective net to Redwood = $0.000246 (i.e., Redwood receives 88% of customer payment).
- Net unit delta vs direct: customer pays ~13.6% more when buying via marketplace unless we take a credit.

Options for parity:
1) Redwood credit: Redwood reduces our list price to compensate so the customer-facing price via marketplace results in the equivalent $0.00028 net to Redwood. This requires finance signoff; we can structure as a one-time marketplace uplift credit or as a tiered uplift across the contract term.
2) Commit uplift: Acme increases committed tokens (e.g., to 35M/month) to move to a deeper discount tier, which can offset the marketplace fee without Redwood taking a margin hit.
3) Hybrid: Redwood offers a small, time-limited credit for the first 3 months while Acme migrates billing to direct for renewals.

Recommendation: For a 12-month, 25M/month commitment I recommend option 1 with a capped marketplace credit so Redwood preserves unit economics after year-1 renewal discussions. If Acme is sensitive to procurement through AWS, we can propose a DocuSign via AWS but include a line item showing the marketplace fee and the applied Redwood credit for transparency.

Action items:
- Rishi: please confirm whether we can approve a marketplace credit that preserves $0.00028 net per token for the first 12 months for the ACME deal and the expected accounting treatment.
- Tessa: if approved, I'll prepare a redline-friendly pricing exhibit that includes the credit language and the invoice flow.

Neha
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarification on per-token discounts via AWS Marketplace vs Direct

Tessa / Neha / Rishi — thanks for the detailed breakdown and options. The worked example is exactly what procurement needed. Two quick follow-ups:

1) We prefer to keep the purchase on AWS Marketplace for compliance reasons, so a marketplace-friendly approach is required.
2) We accept the proposed capped marketplace credit for the first 12 months provided the contract language clearly states the credit amount and the invoice flow via AWS Marketplace.

Please route the DocuSign via AWS Marketplace with the pricing exhibit that documents the credit and the net per-token rate. Once we have a signed agreement we will schedule the onboarding kickoff.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this week.

Regards,
Maya Rao
Procurement Lead
Acme AI
